display_title: Open-Source Infrastructure Query Explorer (OpenStreetMap / Overpass) - prototype
one_liner: A Streamlit and folium front end for OpenStreetMap: basemaps, reverse geocoding, and Overpass lookups of facilities around a point. This is a prototype toward an infrastructure access analysis tool.
problem: Planners often need a fast first look at what infrastructure exists around a location (hospitals, fuel, power, bridges) from open data that is available anywhere. Commercial or classified geospatial holdings may not cover every location or may not be releasable.
approach: The app sends Overpass API queries for OSM amenity nodes within 1 km of a user-set point and Nominatim reverse geocoding. Results appear in a table and on an interactive folium map with drawing and measurement controls.
decision_relevance: Potential: first-look infrastructure IPB (intelligence preparation of the battlefield) or HA/DR site assessment (facility inventory, nearest-facility distance, with coverage caveats). Currently it supports no specific decision; the analysis layer is not built.

headline_results.claim: Queries live OSM data through the Overpass API for amenities near a point, and reverse-geocodes through Nominatim
headline_results.evidence: app.py / app_fixed.py Execute Query handler (Overpass node[amenity](around:1000); Nominatim /reverse)

headline_results.claim: Interactive drawing and distance/area measurement on the map
headline_results.evidence: folium plugins.Draw and plugins.MeasureControl in app.py

limitations: The heatmap is 100 uniformly random points around the map centre, not data.
Queries return nodes only: facilities mapped as ways or relations (most hospitals, schools, parks) are missed. 'park' queries the wrong key (amenity instead of leisure).
The query radius is fixed at 1 km, results are silently cut to 20, and the 'Search Location' option has no handler.
OSM completeness varies by region. No data timestamp or coverage caveat is shown.
Drawn shapes are not read back, so no analysis runs on user areas.
The public app.py still offers deprecated Stamen tiles (3 of 6 styles). The fix exists only in the unversioned app_fixed.py.
Dependencies are unpinned and the code has no license.
blockers_before_featuring: Remove the random heatmap, or replace it with a density of real query results.
Make app_fixed.py the public app.py (Stamen removal), add .gitignore, pin folium/streamlit-folium, and retire the duplicate local copies (osm-explore has an unrelated git history).
Fix 'Search Location' (implement or remove), switch to nwr + out center, fix park=leisure, use HTTPS plus a User-Agent, and stop silent truncation at 20.
Build at least one real analysis output (facility counts per class and nearest-facility distance for a drawn area) before using an ORSA framing.
Show the Overpass timestamp_osm_base and a completeness caveat. Add a Limitations section.
README: replace the <your-repo-url> placeholder and stale folder name; add a code LICENSE, a screenshot and a demo link.
README claims contradicted at HEAD: 'Heatmap visualization' (random data), 'Stamen' tile styles, 'Search Location'.
